feat: publishing AppRouter without hassle
items.body:
### Describe the feature you'd like to request

I am using trpc in bunch of projects that are spread across npm packages. E.g., I have a server `my-server` and a client `my-client`. In `my-client` code I am importing `AppRouter` like this:
```ts
import type { AppRouter } from `my-server`;
```
I want to be able to publish `AppRouter` types on NPM without exposing any sensitive information like my server source code or `Context` of the `AppRouter`.

### Describe the solution you'd like to see

When generating .d.ts files via `tsc` or `vite`, .d.ts files contain all imported type definitions. Since `AppRouter` depends on `Context`, and `Context` usually contains all backend services (e.g., `UsersService`, `PaymentService`, etc), all the backend type declarations are also included in .d.ts files.

I see at least two solutions:
- Somehow replace `Context` object with `unknown` when generating .d.ts files
- If `appRouter` is defined in `src/router.ts`, only include `dist/router.d.ts` in package.json `files` field.

I hope trpc provides a recommended way to publish `AppRouter`, so developers do not need to think about it themselves.

### Describe alternate solutions

Don't provide a recommended way of publishing `AppRouter` and leave it to devs.

### Additional information

_No response_

### 👨‍👧‍👦 Contributing

- [X] 🙋‍♂️ Yes, I'd be down to file a PR implementing this feature!

items.title: feat: add `localLink` / `ssrLink` that runs the router in the same process as the client
items.body:
### Describe the feature you'd like to request

Hi there!

It would be great to have a `LocalLink` that allows me to do:
This would directly run the router in the same process as the client instead of transferring requests to a server.

### But why??

This is motivated mainly due to testing and fast prototyping:
1. This allows to test the client with the server code (with a small caveat, see below)
2. I can start writing a fully functional client that saves data in local storage instead of a database, and when I want to add a database, I don't need to rewrite the procedures, giving me significantly faster prototyping speed.

### Describe the solution you'd like to see

```ts
import { createRouter } from '../path/to/server/trpc';
const client = createTRPCProxyClient<ReturnType<typeof createRouter>>({
  links: [
    localLink({ router: createRouter({ database }) }),
  ],
});```

For the feature itself it doesn't matter that the router is created by a function call, but this solves a problem I mentioned above: What if part of the code only runs on the server, e.g. database access? Well, just inject that dependency, and, in case you are running on the client, use a browser-based database.

### Describe alternate solutions

Not sure, to be honest.

### Additional information

_No response_

### 👨‍👧‍👦 Contributing

- [X] 🙋‍♂️ Yes, I'd be down to file a PR implementing this feature!

<sub>[TRP-48](https://linear.app/trpc/issue/TRP-48/feat-add-locallink-that-runs-the-router-in-the-same-process-as-the)</sub>

items.title: feat: Lazy load routers
items.body:
### Describe the feature you'd like to request

Basically `next/dynamic` but for the backend. 

Recently our tRPC router has been growing significantly for many reasons but mostly due to heavy third party SDKs. The problem with this is that even if we're not calling that specific procedure we still load ALL the router dependencies when calling any procedure.

This impacts performance and cold boots significantly.

### Describe the solution you'd like to see

Splitting big tRPC routers into lazy loadable chunks could help loading only what is needed when a procedure is called. I would imagine some pseudo code like this:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3504472/229645485-315a4d62-2044-49ef-b420-0b33bf7fd503.png)


### Describe alternate solutions

Other aternatives involve moving all the procedure code into a separate file a use imports for that [as done in here](https://github.com/calcom/cal.com/pull/7889/commits/6ce440851e172db3f4c7ae720e8396c9201eb316).

Also [lazy loading only third party libraries](https://github.com/calcom/cal.com/pull/7889/commits/a2ff4d9a0cac732af3cd842988feaad471187488) (like Stripe, Google, etc.) seems to help. But it would be a much nicer DX being able to simply lazy load full routers and support it natively.

### Additional information

_No response_

### 👨‍👧‍👦 Contributing

- [X] 🙋‍♂️ Yes, I'd be down to file a PR implementing this feature!

<sub>[TRP-19](https://linear.app/trpc/issue/TRP-19/feat-lazy-load-routers)</sub>

items.title: Different types of `middlewareMarker`
items.body:
Hello,

We have two separate folder for backend and frontend in our repo (no workspace setup) as they are compiled in their respective directories.

In an attempt to introduce `trpc` I stumbled upon an issue that we have two copies of `@trpc/server` package - both in server's and in client's `node_modules`.
The problem is that when I import `AppRouter` type from the server to client - I get a type mismatch of the `middlewareMarker` which is a symbol created in [middlewares.ts](https://github.com/trpc/trpc/blob/4c91e920529daa4f7c1a88cbc7b0db8a5ed405ce/packages/server/src/internals/middlewares.ts#L4).
It seems like I have two symbols that are by definition different.

Is it intended to be so?
Do I have to migrate to common `node_modules` (via workspaces) or there is a way around it?

The code:
```ts
// backend/index.ts
import * as trpc from "trpc/server";

const router = trpc.router();
export type AppRouter = typeof router;
```

```ts
// frontend/index.ts
import {createReactQueryHooks} from "@trpc/react";
import type { AppRouter } from "../backend/index";

export const trpc = createReactQueryHooks<AppRouter>();
```

The error:
```ts
(property) BaseHandlerOptions<AnyRouter<any>, e.Request<ParamsDictionary, any, any, QueryString.ParsedQs, Record<string, any>>>.router: AnyRouter<any>
Type 'Router<Context, Context, {}, Record<"path", Procedure<Context, Context, {}, undefined, undefined, BlockView, unknown, BlockView>>, Record<...> & ... 37 more ... & Record<...>, Record<...>, DefaultErrorShape>' is not assignable to type 'AnyRouter<any>'.
  The types of '_def.middlewares' are incompatible between these types.
    Type 'MiddlewareFunction<Context, Context, {}>[]' is not assignable to type 'MiddlewareFunction<any, any, any>[]'.
      Type 'MiddlewareFunction<Context, Context, {}>' is not assignable to type 'MiddlewareFunction<any, any, any>'.
        Types of parameters 'opts' and 'opts' are incompatible.
          Type '{ ctx: any; type: ProcedureType; path: string; rawInput: unknown; meta?: any; next: { (): Promise<MiddlewareResult<any>>; <T>(opts: { ctx: T; }): Promise<MiddlewareResult<T>>; }; }' is not assignable to type '{ ctx: Context; type: ProcedureType; path: string; rawInput: unknown; meta?: {} | undefined; next: { (): Promise<MiddlewareResult<Context>>; <T>(opts: { ...; }): Promise<...>; }; }'.
            The types returned by 'next()' are incompatible between these types.
              Type 'Promise<MiddlewareResult<any>>' is not assignable to type 'Promise<MiddlewareResult<Context>>'.
                Type 'MiddlewareResult<any>' is not assignable to type 'MiddlewareResult<Context>'.
                  Type 'MiddlewareOKResult<any>' is not assignable to type 'MiddlewareResult<Context>'.
                    Type 'MiddlewareOKResult<any>' is not assignable to type 'MiddlewareOKResult<Context>'.
                      Types of property 'marker' are incompatible.
                        Type 'typeof import("/.../backend/node_modules/@trpc/server/dist/declarations/src/internals/middlewares").middlewareMarker' is not assignable to type 'typeof import("/.../frontend/node_modules/@trpc/server/dist/declarations/src/internals/middlewares").middlewareMarker'.ts(2322)

items.title: feat: Allow subset of router's context when creating SSG helpers
items.body:
## 🎯 Changes

This change infers the given context type when creating SSG helpers. The inferred type must be a subset of the router's context, otherwise the user will see the following error message via the type error:

"_The context you have given is either not a direct match or not a subset of the router's context._"

### Why I want this

- In my router context, I want to set the Next.js `req` and `res` , so I can easily use it in my procedures (e.g. for auth).
- I want to use SSG helpers for both `getServerSideProps` and also `getStaticProps`.


This setup means that some context usages have `req` & `res` and some have not.
I created an inner context creator to mitigate that:

```ts
export async function createContextTRPCInner() {
  return {
    prisma,
  }
}

export async function createContextTRPC(opts: CreateNextContextOptions) {
  const contextInner = await createContextTRPCInner()

  return {
    ...contextInner,
    req: opts.req,
    res: opts.res,
  }
}

export type ContextTRPC = inferAsyncReturnType<typeof createContextTRPC>
```

I use `createContextTRPC` for my routers, as they all have `req` & `res`.

I **wanted** to use `createContextTRPCInner` for the cases where I don't have `req` & `res`, but it won't work: When using `createProxySSGHelpers`, it expects to be passed the context.
But right now, it infers the context type directly from the router, see https://github.com/trpc/trpc/blob/main/packages/react-query/src/ssg/ssg.ts#L20.

### Result of this change

This change will instead infer the context from the giving parameters of `createProxySSGHelpers`.

Here's the error message shown to the user when he tries to give a context that is not a subset of the router's context:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/29319414/205141978-56f0a60f-96c3-4a30-a96d-9a53b5631d49.png)

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/29319414/205142042-a25a3a4b-cbee-43fe-8e7a-c3365f1f293c.png)




### Open topics

- [ ] There's an error shown [in the test I've added](https://github.com/trpc/trpc/blob/3c69cc0643a6e131d87a5d277b3d0165828a6f04/packages/tests/server/react/ssg.test.ts#L14) in my editor, but I don't know what it means:
  
  ![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/29319414/205142162-1630d831-92d6-4ba5-b7e8-79ef0c13dd90.png)



## ✅ Checklist

- [x] I have followed the steps listed in the [Contributing guide](https://github.com/trpc/trpc/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [ ] If necessary, I have added documentation related to the changes made.
- [x] I have added or updated the tests related to the changes made.

items.title: feat: Definitive declaration of context types
items.body:
### Describe the feature you'd like to request

I am currently writing an API with trpc, and I am using `ctx` to pass down a user object once an auth header is being sent to the server. However, I am always falling back to using `ctx.user!.id` because the user attribute *can be* (but not must be) `null`/`undefined`.

Is there a way to strictly typing the context for specific routers?

### Describe the solution you'd like to see

I'd love to see a solution for typing the context for different behaviors. Or at least, when there is a middleware, and the middleware is checking for existence of any context variable, so that the context is being "re-typed" with the checked presence in the middleware.

### Desribe alternate solutions

As written above, I am currently using `ctx.user!.id`, which **is working**, but is not ideal.

### Additional information

_No response_

items.body:
For our application, we have a use case where the URL for the websocket api can change, and so our solution has been to treat the trpc client as state, and change it whenever the url changes. However, whenever we change it, there are pending connections that stay in the background. 

Is this use case supported?
If not, is there some easy workaround we could do by calling internals?

Thanks
